newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: GOLF-GARRIDO MAINTAINS PUSH FOR RYDER CUP PLACE.
newsitem.headline: GOLF-GARRIDO MAINTAINS PUSH FOR RYDER CUP PLACE.

text.p: Ignacio Garrido maintained his push for a Ryder Cup place by moving to within two strokes of the lead in the Czech Open on Thursday to capture a share of third place behind front-runner Scott Henderson.
Henderson fired a course record-equalling seven-under-par 64 to finish the first round one stroke ahead of fellow Briton Simon Hurley.

A fine back nine of four birdies after faltering early on, showed Garrido had not lost the form which won him his first European Tour event eight weeks ago, the German Open, and second place in last week's Scandinavian Masters.

The 25-year-old from Madrid, 10th in the Ryder Cup standings, scrambled a birdie at the first after being bunkered but then bogeyed the short third and had to work hard for pars around a second birdie on the sixth.
But once Garrido had settled down, his putter produced more birdies instead of just saving pars.
"I'm playing well but putting even better," said the Spaniard who was invited only on Monday to play the final major, the U.S. PGA championship.
"It will be a bonus by giving me an extra chance for Ryder Cup points. I can make it into the team easily if I don't keep thinking about it on the course and save it until after the round."
Henderson, a qualifier from the European Tour school last year, took the lead with an eagle and six birdies with one dropped shot.
Former world tennis number one Ivan Lendl, playing his second Czech Open as a pro, started brightly but slumped to an 82, a repeat of his opening round last year in Marianske Lazne.
